notes: Author claims: the two displayed axioms govern the map d and the action denoted by a barred oval. The following paragraph asserts invariance of Im d, defines pi_0 as the cokernel, says pi_1=Ker d is central in L_1, and says L_0 acts on L_1 preserving pi_1 and acts via pi_0. These assertions are transcribed, not independently proved.

Author claim: the principal invariant, with coh. added above the line, is the Postnikoff/Postnikuff–Sinh class alpha in H^3(pi_0,pi_1). The possible point after membership is a documentary uncertainty, not a mathematical correction.

Author narrative: he has met these structures in various situations and recently again in the classification of ordinary formal groups over a perfect field, expressed using affine algebraic groups, commutative formal groups and strict Gr-structures. The final quotation continues beyond this sheet.

Page identification: the visible author number is 5 and the pencil archive foliation is 150. H’s editorial page 149 is not substituted for either visible number. No date, salutation or closing appears on this continuation page.

Reader observations: all mathematical glyph occurrences were read independently. Repeated barred ovals and pi-family roofs were not copied from a notation-table decision. The unfamiliar d. before an opening parenthesis, the exact en invariant wording, and qu’il opère via pi_0 prompted close ink inspection and were retained without repair.

Reader observations: ordinary line-by-line inspection is not a proof event. No targeted proof, re-proof, computation or mathematical refutation was performed; checks is therefore empty. No author assertion is certified by this reading.

Author doubt language: no explicit author query or stated mathematical doubt appears on this sheet; évidemment is an assertion of obviousness. The editorial doubt macros here express reader uncertainty only.

Layout/state observations: this is an entirely handwritten continuation page. There are no mathematical diagrams or drawings. The marginal guide arrow is a textual annotation guide and is recorded with the margin note, not invented as a mathematical arrow. The first line of that note is physically depleted. The exact attachment of the note and the correction state at sur remain uncertain.

coverage: The whole 1681 × 2365 image was viewed once for layout, then half a and half b once each, sequentially and line by line against both complete witness texts. The opening continuation, every line of both axiom explanations/displays, every line of the properties paragraph, the coh. insertion, the full central formula, every lower prose line, all quotations, punctuation, word endings, accents, indices, parentheses, underlines, corrections, the sideways marginal note and both page-number systems were inspected. Fifteen tight crops were made only for loci left unresolved by those halves, with no re-crop of a decided locus; the long margin crop was rotated upright. The overlap was not used to create an additional half enlargement. Every C doubt has a resolution or retained-doubt entry. The report records the witness differences including the cancelled sign and d-point omitted by H, vais/sais, the affines comma, actual quotation shapes, margin ce/le and placement, and the unresolved final du/des. H’s acknowledgement of the pale clipped marginal line and of page numbers is not falsely counted as an omission. The possible deleted substrate before sur is represented with an outer state doubt. No other page, reader output, root decision, OCR, external source, or LaTeX compilation was used.
